memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Judah said to Onan, 'Sleep with your brother's wife and fulfill your duty to her as a brother-in-law to raise up offspring for your brother.' But Onan knew that the child would not be his; so whenever he slept with his brother's wife, he spilled his semen on the ground to keep from providing offspring for his brother. What he did was wicked in the LORD's sight; so the LORD put him to death also." - Gen 38:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Er dies childless, Judah tells his second son, Onan, to fulfill an ancient duty: to father a child with Tamar who would carry on his dead brother's name and provide for the widow. This custom, later written into Israel's law, protected vulnerable widows and preserved a family line. But Onan wanted none of it.

Onan was willing to use Tamar for his own pleasure, but he refused to give her the child that was her due and his brother's right. He wanted the benefit without the responsibility, taking for himself while giving nothing back. The Bible calls this "wicked in the LORD's sight." At the heart of Onan's sin was cold selfishness — he exploited Tamar while deliberately denying his dead brother an heir and Tamar her security.

This exposes a sin that can hide in any of us: the willingness to take what we want from others while shirking what we owe them. We can use people for our own benefit — their help, their affection, their labour — while refusing to give what love and duty require. That is selfishness dressed up as relationship.

God calls us to the opposite. Real love "does not seek its own" (1 Cor 13:5) but gives, serves, and honours our obligations to others. Ask God to root out any selfishness that takes without giving, and to make you a person who faithfully gives others their due.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I tempted to take from others while shirking what I owe them?
2. Do I use people for my benefit, or truly serve them?
3. How can I be more faithful to my duties toward others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, root out the selfishness that takes without giving. Teach me to love others truly — to serve them, honour my duties, and seek their good rather than only my own. Amen.
